                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1762,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"                  \\\"content\\\": \\\"The navigation overlay only shows when the route is not reversed, causing incoherent UI when flipped. Also, route caching keys ignore direction, risking mismatched cached routes when isRouteReversed changes, which can cause the displayed route and ghost to be out of sync unless always recalculated on toggle.&amp;amp;lt;/details&amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;lt;/think&amp;amp;gt;\\\"\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1770,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"                  \\\"content\\\": \\\"The route request properly flips endpoints using isRouteReversed, but the ghost always calculates progress from the device perspective without flipping, causing mismatched ghost direction when reversed. The navigation overlay is disabled when reversed rather than flipped, so no overlay shows for user-&amp;amp;gt;device mode. Route caching keys omit direction, risking reuse of routes for the wrong direction and causing ghost and progress inconsistencies. These combined gaps create incoherent flipping behavior despite the requirement that route, ghost, and overlay flip together.&amp;amp;lt;/details&amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;lt;/think&amp;amp;gt;\\\"\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1782,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"                  \\\"content\\\": \\\"The ghost logic explicitly stays in **device perspective** even when the route is reversed. When &amp;amp;#96;isRouteReversed == false&amp;amp;#96; (user → device), it still treats the device as the “start” of travel (i.e., ghost moves *from device toward user*), and it swaps done/todo segments to match the device perspective.  \\\"\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1806,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"                  \\\"content\\\": \\\"**Effect:** On view appear (or auto‑updates), a cached user→device route can be reused even when &amp;amp;#96;isRouteReversed == true&amp;amp;#96;, causing ghost/progress logic to operate with the *wrong* assumption about polyline direction.\\\"\""
                },

                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 5708,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"The route request properly flips endpoints using isRouteReversed, but the ghost always calculates progress from the device perspective without flipping, causing mismatched ghost direction when reversed.                 {
                  "lineNumber": 25422,
                  "content": "  \"plan\": \"# Plan: Reverse Navigation Double-Tap Mode\\n\\n## Zielbild\\n\\nWenn ein User im Reverse-Navigations-Modus (&amp;#96;isRouteReversed == true&amp;#96;) per Double-Tap die Karte auf Navigation schaltet, sollen folgende Änderungen aktiviert werden:\\n\\n- **User-Location-Annotation mit Blickrichtungspfeil**: Custom-Annotation mit Richtungspfeil, der die aktuelle Blickrichtung anzeigt und korrekt rotiert (berücksichtigt Kartenrotation)\\n- **Kartenrotation**: Die Karte rotiert um die Blickrichtung des Users während der Navigation\\n- **Follow-Camera**: Kamera folgt dem User mit weichen Animationen\\n- **Initiale Sequenz**: Route wird gefittet, dann nach 2.5s in den Navigation-Look gezoomt\\n\\n## Aktuelle Situation\\n\\n- &amp;#96;handleMapDoubleTap()&amp;#96; funktioniert nur wenn &amp;#96;!isRouteReversed&amp;#96; ist (Zeile 1115)\\n- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; hat keine Heading-Logik (nur Course aus &amp;#96;currentLocation?.course&amp;#96;)\\n- &amp;#96;userMarkerContent&amp;#96; verwendet &amp;#96;MiataruMapMarker&amp;#96; ohne Heading [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 25995,
                  "content": "Updated the marker swap condition so the heading-style marker is only used when the route is shown from the user device to the other device (&#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;). All other modes keep the standard marker."
                }
              ]
            },
            {
              "file": "./.cursor/plans/reverse_navigation_double-tap_mode_241b4efc.plan.md",

                  "lineNumber": 6337,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"The navigation overlay only shows when the route is not reversed, causing incoherent UI when flipped. Also, route caching keys ignore direction, risking mismatched cached routes when isRouteReversed changes, which can cause the displayed route and ghost to be out of sync unless always recalculated on toggle.&amp;lt;/details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/think&amp;gt;\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 6345,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"The route request properly flips endpoints using isRouteReversed, but the ghost always calculates progress from the device perspective without flipping, causing mismatched ghost direction when reversed. The navigation overlay is disabled when reversed rather than flipped, so no overlay shows for user-&amp;gt;device mode. Route caching keys omit direction, risking reuse of routes for the wrong direction and causing ghost and progress inconsistencies. These combined gaps create incoherent flipping behavior despite the requirement that route, ghost, and overlay flip together.&amp;lt;/details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/think&amp;gt;\""
                },

                  "lineNumber": 6357,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"The ghost logic explicitly stays in **device perspective** even when the route is reversed.                 },

                  "content": "The navigation overlay only shows when the route is not reversed, causing incoherent UI when flipped. <think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>

I see the issue. In the current code:
- Line 53: `@State private var isRouteReversed: Bool = true // Default: device to user` — So when true it says "device to user". But user said Reversed = User → device. So the comment is wrong: when isRouteReversed is true it should be "user to device" (reversed route), and default when they press "navigate" is... Let me check. User said: "Non-Reversed Route = standard navigation = The route from the selected Device to the user-device. It's shown when the user selects 'navigate'." So default (when you first navigate) = device → user = non-reversed. Summary of what was committed:

**Commit:** `773ffd7b` — *Navigation: double-tap focus only when reversed route; align reversed/non-reversed naming*

**1. Double-tap and chrome**
- **Double-tap** only does something when the route is **reversed** (user → selected device). When the route is non-reversed (device → user), double-tap has no effect.
- **Entering** focussed navigation (double-tap): chrome is hidden (same as a single tap on the NavigationOverlayKit instructions).
- **Leaving** (double-tap again or navigation ends): chrome is shown again (toolbars and tab bar).

**2. Route direction naming and docs**
- **State:** `isRouteReversed` was renamed to **`isRouteFromDeviceToUser`** in `iPhone_DeviceNavigationView`.
  - `true` = non-reversed (standard: device → user)
  - `false` = reversed (user → device, “reverse route” button)
- **Comments and docs** now consistently use:
  - **Reversed route** = user → selected device
  - **Non-reversed route** = selected device → user
- **Logic:** Double-tap runs only when `!isRouteFromDeviceToUser` (reversed). Navigation feedback (voice/haptics) also only when reversed.
- **RouteGhostCalculator** and **RouteCacheStore:** parameter meaning documented; call sites use the label `isRouteReversed:` and pass `isRouteFromDeviceToUser`.

**Files in the commit:**  
`iPhone_DeviceNavigationView.swift`, `RouteGhostCalculator.swift`, `RouteCacheStore.swift` (3 files, +36 / -32 lines).
